the `if (state?.teamId)` branch writes a team-wide `Credential` row after checking only `accepted: true` membership, with no role predicate. `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` sits in the fall-through branch, which is only reachable when `teamId` is falsy, so it is always called with `null` and guards nothing. Any accepted member -- including a plain MEMBER -- can install team-wide OAuth credentials. Move the admin call above the branch so it runs on both paths.

when a provider response omits `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal 8-character string `"refresh_token"`. Office365 spreads that over the stored credential and persists it, destroying a working refresh token; the next refresh POSTs the placeholder and fails permanently, so the user must reconnect. In sync mode this is deterministic rather than occasional, because #3 strips `refresh_token` unconditionally. Delete the fallback and preserve the caller's previous value instead.

`z.string().toString()` is not a zod catch-all; it is `Object.prototype.toString`, so both computed keys evaluate to the same literal `"[object Object]"` and the second overwrites the first. The validator confirmed empirically against zod that the schema reduces to `{access_token, "[object Object]"}` and that parsing a realistic token response returns only `{access_token}`. Every expiry, refresh token and provider field is silently dropped -- and because it accepts `{access_token: ""}`, a garbage sync response validates clean. This is the root cause of #2's determinism and of the Salesforce and Office365 field loss. Use an explicit shape plus `.passthrough()`.

the sync branch returns an undici `Response`; the fallback returns whatever the app's own refresh call produced. The `refreshFunction: () => any` signature erases the difference, so TypeScript stays green while six consumers read fields that do not exist. There is also no `response.ok` check, so a 500 from the sync endpoint flows onward as success. Give the helper one declared, parsed return type -- that single decision resolves #8, #9, #12 and #13.

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `SafeParseReturnType`, but this call site assigns it straight into `data: { key }`. The previous line used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the data. So the next token refresh writes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` into `credential.key` and the Google integration breaks for that user on the following request. **This fires with credential sync switched off** -- it is not gated behind the new feature.

grep finds exactly one occurrence of `prisma` in this file: the usage on line 96. The import block has no `@calcom/prisma` binding. That is a TS2304 compile error, or a `ReferenceError` on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction if the build emits anyway. **Also not gated behind the feature flag.** That no CI gate caught a missing import in a changed file is itself worth a look.

the only authentication on an endpoint that writes OAuth credentials for an arbitrary `userId` is `!==` between a header and an env var, with no non-emptiness assertion on either side. `.env.example` ships `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""`, so an operator who enables credential sharing but leaves the secret blank gets `undefined !== undefined`, which is false, and a request with no header at all is accepted. Reachability depends on how `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is derived, which is outside this checkout -- hence anchor 75 rather than 100. Fail closed on missing config, lowercase the header name, and compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

a `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` is `undefined` and the next line throws. The resulting `TypeError` message is not `"invalid_grant"`, so the existing catch swallows it and returns the stale auth object -- the refresh silently does nothing. Resolved by #4.

same root cause, worse outcome: `expiresIn` is `undefined` on a `Response`, so `expiryDate` becomes `NaN`, and the `Response` instance itself is written to `credential.key` via `key: hubspotRefreshToken as any`. A `Response` has no own enumerable properties, so the stored credential serializes to roughly `{}` and the connection is unrecoverable without reconnecting. Resolved by #4, but validate the shape at this call site too.

`getClient` runs a full OAuth round-trip to `login.salesforce.com` plus a `prisma.credential.update` on every instantiation, with no expiry gate. Every sibling integration touched in this same diff keeps its guard (`isExpired`, `isTokenValid`, `isTokenExpiring`); Salesforce alone lost it. That is added latency and a write on every booking and availability operation, plus rate-limit exposure. `salesforceTokenSchema` already captures `issued_at` -- store an expiry and gate on it.

this is the umbrella coverage gap. A new externally reachable endpoint that decrypts and writes into the `credential` table has zero tests across all ~7 branches. Narrower per-branch gaps are listed under Coverage. Cover at minimum: disabled flag, secret mismatch, unset secret, malformed body, unknown user/app slug, decrypt failure, and both the create and update paths.

three call sites were routed through `refreshOAuthTokens` but not given the companion `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so they still decode with provider-specific logic the sync payload cannot satisfy: lark expects a nested `data.data.*`, webex's schema requires `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`, and office365video persists `responseBody` wholesale. Either parse at all three sites and merge onto the existing key, or fall through to `refreshFunction()` for apps the sync endpoint cannot drive.

this fetch is awaited inside the token-refresh path of every wrapped integration, which is itself on booking-critical operations. No `AbortSignal`, no status check: a hung sync endpoint blocks the calendar request until the platform timeout, and a 5xx is treated as a successful refresh. Distinct fix from #4 -- add the timeout even after the return shape is settled.

the diff deletes the `console.error(... zodError, MS response ...)` block, and the shared helper now throws a generic `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` carrying neither the zod error nor the provider response. What was a deliberate log-and-continue degrade with the still-valid prior credentials is now an opaque throw. Whether it takes down a whole multi-calendar availability call could not be confirmed from this checkout -- see Coverage. Restore the diagnostic and decide deliberately whether this should fail only the one integration.

`credentialKey` is captured before the new refresh block, and the connection is built from it afterwards. The freshly minted token is written to the database but never used for the request in flight, so the refresh is a no-op for the current call. Build the connection from `accessTokenParsed.data`.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — No method guard, no input error handling, and an empty-string encryption-key fallback

five reviewers landed here independently. The 93-line handler has no `try`/`catch`: `.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on a malformed body, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a wrong or absent key -- `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` hands AES-256 a zero-length key, which Node rejects. There is also no `req.method` check, so any verb runs the full DB-write path. The result is 500s with stack traces where the file's own 403/404 branches establish a clean JSON error convention. Fail fast above the two prisma lookups: 405 on non-POST, a named 500 when the key is unset, `safeParse` into a 400, and a try/catch around decrypt.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Webhook secret check passes when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset or empty

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check is `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (i.e., `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is `undefined`), and the request omits the header, `req.headers[...]` is also `undefined`, so the comparison is `undefined !== undefined` which is false, meaning the code does NOT return 403 and the request is accepted. This makes the webhook effectively unauthenticated when the env var is not set. (The 'empty string' case only passes if the header is explicitly the empty string, but the 'unset' case is a clear bypass.)

In JavaScript, those expressions are evaluated immediately to a single string key (typically `"[object Object]"`), they do not create a Zod “catch-all”/index signature. packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Reads `res?.data` off a raw fetch `Response` in sync mode

adjudication.rationale:
In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code was changed to:

```ts
const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...);
const token = res?.data;
```

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns different types depending on mode:
- Normal mode: it returns whatever the provided `refreshFunction` returns. Here the refresh function returns `fetchTokens.res`, which (from Google auth libs) is typically a gaxios-style response with a `.data` field.
- Sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`): it performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw Fetch API `Response` object.

A Fetch `Response` does not have a `.data` property; its body must be read via `await res.json()` (or similar). Therefore, in sync mode `token` becomes `undefined`, leading to `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date` being incorrect and likely throwing at runtime.

This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff (new `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` + updated `CalendarService.ts`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — No method guard, no input error handling, and an empty-string encryption-key fallback

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` does not check `req.method`, so it will process non-POST requests as long as headers/body are present. It also uses `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` without a try/catch; Zod `parse` throws on invalid input, which will result in an unhandled exception (500) rather than a controlled 4xx response. Finally, it calls `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`, meaning if the encryption key env var is missing it silently falls back to an empty string key, which is a verifiable correctness/security defect (decryption may fail or operate with an unintended weak/invalid key) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: five reviewers landed here independently. The 93-line handler has no `try`/`catch`: `.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on a malformed body, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a wrong or absent key -- `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` hands AES-256 a zero-length key, which Node rejects. There is also no `req.method` check, so any verb runs the full DB-write path. The result is 500s with stack traces where the file's own 403/404 branches establish a clean JSON error convention. Fail fast above the two prisma lookups: 405 on non-POST, a named 500 when the key is unset, `safeParse` into a 400, and a try/catch around decrypt.
